name: Tricentis Tosca
tagline: Model-based, low-code test automation for enterprise apps including SAP, mainframes, and thick clients.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Tricentis does not publish Tosca list pricing, it is quote-based enterprise licensing.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely one-shot a test runner. Playwright plus a YAML test spec plus an HTML report is a comfortable afternoon, and for a web app you own, that is genuinely all you need. What Tosca sells is the part nobody wants to write: scanning and modeling SAP GUI screens, Siebel, Oracle Forms, mainframe green screens, Citrix-published desktop apps, and keeping those object models stable across vendor upgrades. Add risk-based test selection, audit trails that satisfy a pharma validation auditor, and a licensing structure that lets a QA manager point at one vendor when a release breaks. A personal replacement is fine for your own web app and irrelevant to the thing Tosca is actually bought for.
coreLoopDIY: Runs YAML-defined browser test cases against your web app with reusable page modules and spits out a local HTML report with screenshots on failure.
requirements: A web app with stable selectors or data-testid attributes
Willingness to maintain your own selectors forever
whatYouLose: Scanning and object modeling for SAP, mainframe, Citrix, and other non-web interfaces, which is most of why Tosca exists
Risk-based test case design and coverage analytics across thousands of cases
Vendor-maintained steering for apps that change under you, so every selector break is now your problem
Audit trails, electronic signatures, and validation packs for regulated industries
Anything resembling enterprise support when a release is blocked at 2am
moatNotes: The real asset is the technology adapters: the ability to drive an SAP GUI or a 3270 terminal as reliably as a web page. That is years of grinding against closed interfaces, not a weekend of prompting.
whyPeopleStillPay: Nobody buys Tosca to test a React app. They buy it because they have a twenty-year-old SAP install, a Siebel instance, two thick clients, and an auditor who wants a signed trace from requirement to test result. Tosca drives interfaces that have no public automation API, keeps those models working through vendor upgrades, and gives a QA organization a single throat to choke. Building adapters for even one of those surfaces is a multi-year engineering program, and the compliance paperwork is not something you generate from a prompt.
notes: A Playwright wrapper is a weekend; an SAP GUI adapter is not. The moat is the technology adapters for interfaces with no public automation API, plus the validation paperwork that regulated buyers legally need.
prompt:
Build a local, dependency-light browser test runner called "tosca-lite" in an empty folder.

Stack, no alternatives: Node.js 20 ESM, TypeScript, Playwright (chromium only by default), yaml for parsing, no test framework, no cloud, no accounts, no telemetry.

What it does:
1. Reads test cases from ./tests/*.yaml. Each file declares: name, baseUrl (or reads BASE_URL from .env), and steps.
2. Supports reusable "modules": ./modules/*.yaml files that define named step sequences with parameters, so a login flow is written once and referenced by many tests. This is the one Tosca idea worth copying: steps are data, not code.
3. Step verbs, keep exactly this set: goto, click, fill, select, waitFor, expectText, expectVisible, expectUrl, screenshot, use (invokes a module with params).
4. Selectors resolve in this order: data-testid, role+name, then raw CSS. Fail loudly on ambiguous matches instead of picking the first.
5. CLI: `npm run test` runs everything, `npm run test -- --file tests/login.yaml` runs one, `--headed` disables headless, `--grep` filters by test name.
6. On failure, capture a full-page screenshot plus the page HTML into ./artifacts/{test}/{step}/ and continue to the next test.
7. Emit ./artifacts/report.html: a single self-contained file listing each test, each step, pass/fail, duration, and inline failure screenshots. No JS frameworks, just plain HTML and inline CSS.
8. Exit code 1 if any test failed, so it drops into CI unchanged.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build: SAP, Citrix, mainframe, or any desktop automation; record-and-playback; a GUI editor; risk-based test selection; user management; any hosted dashboard.

Deliver: README with a 60-second quickstart, .env.example containing BASE_URL, two example tests and one example login module, and a .gitignore that excludes artifacts/ and .env.
